# Awesome DIY Learning

**Learn by Making, Exploring, Repairing, and Experimenting.**

A library of free project-based learning for curious people: stitch a notebook, build a mechanism, paint a leaf, grow something, or put an old object back into use. Pick something small and enjoyable. There are no deadlines, scores, or pressure to turn a hobby into work.

Curiosity comes first. We value clear instructions, original creators, traditional craftsmanship and modern technology. Free learning means the instructions are accessible; tools, supplies, replacement parts and workshop access may still cost money.

## Read the labels

**Free access:** `open` = instruction available without an account; `free-registration` = a free account is needed; `mixed` = the linked free instruction sits beside paid extras; `restricted-free-tier` = software or service limits apply; `unverified` = a research lead whose current access needs checking. None of these promises free materials. Access notes explain the particular restriction.

**Review level:** `source-checked` identifies an offering and its free content; `sample-reviewed` records inspection of one complete representative project; `build-tested` requires a contributor's actual completion report. No initial entry is build-tested. Imported source checks are explicitly attributed to the initial research in the migration audit and do not establish current availability.

**Editorial disposition:** category tables contain `listed` resources with current publisher evidence. `needs-review` entries stay in the queue; `reference-only` entries provide context or discovery rather than a complete make; `excluded` entries retain an auditable reason. A passing HTTP check establishes reachability only.

**Format and approach are different.** Format says how instruction is delivered: article, video, PDF, patterns, interactive exercises, course or project library. Approach says what you do: build, experiment, design, repair or solve a lab. See all ten approaches in the [data model](docs/data-model.md#learning-approaches).

Difficulty, duration, language, cost and equipment are recorded only when supported. **Unknown means unknown.** A library-level beginner label applies to its representative project, not every item in the library.

## Learn by repairing

Repair is a first-class way to learn materials, mechanisms and troubleshooting. Explore [mending, bicycles, hand tools, furniture, computers and outdoor gear](categories/repair-and-restoration.md). Records support object type, activity, device specificity, parts, reversibility, risk and checks after repair.

Start with a small non-critical object and matching instructions. Back up computer data; disconnect power as the guide directs; keep fasteners organized. Leave mains appliances, CRTs, microwaves, damaged batteries, pressurized equipment and structural safety repairs to trained specialists. Stored energy can remain after unplugging. Test function after reassembly, and seek qualified help for brakes, steering or load-bearing repairs. See [safety guidance](docs/safety.md).

## Use the data and tools

[data/resources.json](data/resources.json) is the only resource source of truth. JSON keeps loading and generation in Python's standard library; one dependency provides complete JSON Schema validation. No website framework or paid service is required.

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python scripts/validate.py
python scripts/generate.py
python scripts/generate.py --check
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
# Optional: polite, advisory network check; never removes entries.
python scripts/check_links.py --limit 10
```

Use Python 3.11 or newer. CI runs schema checks, tests, generated-file checks and local Markdown link checks on pushes and pull requests. The separate manual link workflow respects robots rules, limits requests and uploads an advisory report. [Schema](schema/resource.schema.json) · [Data model](docs/data-model.md) · [Migration audit](docs/migration.md) · [Validation report](docs/validation.md)

## Limits and credit

The initial catalogue research includes twelve craft expansions and a repair section. Original tutorial URLs and resource occurrences are retained in the dataset. The [migration audit](docs/migration.md) records the import, merges, corrected links and unresolved claims.

The catalogue is intentionally broad but uneven. All 101 originally queued sources received an editorial review attempt; unresolved access, completeness and safety questions remain in the queue. Many listed libraries still need a complete representative-project review, and account-gated lessons and full videos have not all been inspected. External sites change, regional access differs and automated checks can be blocked. Safety notes are editorial prompts, not training. There is no claim that all linked content is equally suitable, that every language is known, or that any project has been personally completed.

Original authors keep all rights to their tutorials, videos, photographs, patterns and books. Follow their licenses and credit them when sharing your work. We link to instruction rather than rehosting it. Repository code is [MIT licensed](LICENSE); original catalogue text and metadata are [CC0 1.0](LICENSE-DATA). These licenses **do not cover external instructional works or quoted source descriptions**. See [licensing boundaries](docs/licensing.md).
